To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a robot learning from demonstration system that can learn from demonstrations, and that we have demonstrated that our system can learn a model and policy for the pendulum swing-up task.

we have developed a novel learning from demonstration approach that is able to learn a task model from demonstration and then use this task model for planning and control of the task, and we have demonstrated that the approach is able to learn from demonstration a task model that allows for the task to be completed in a reasonable amount of time.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework for learning from demon strations of robot tasks that can be applied to a wide range of tasks.

the development of methods for the acquisition of knowledge from human demonstrations of a task and for the subsequent execution of the task by a robot The goal of this research is to develop methods for learning and execution that are robust to the uncertainty and variability inherent in the human demonstration of a task The approach that we take is to use the human demonstration to construct a model of the task and then to use the constructed model to guide the learning and the execution of the task

the development of a general purpose learning from demonstration system that will be useful for a wide variety of robot tasks and that will be able to learn from a single demonstration of an arbitrary task The system will have to be able to handle a wide variety of different tasks and to learn the appropriate reward function and task models for each of these tasks.
